name: Travel Planner by Gildhart
changelog:
• Licence keys. Gildhart gives each client or community member a key for their site's address. With it, the planner shows to everyone (once "Show the planner to everyone" is ticked) and each new version installs itself; without one, it is a preview for the site's editors and takes no updates, and the settings screen and an admin notice say why. Keys are checked inside the plugin against Gildhart's public key, so nothing is ever sent anywhere, and a key is not a secret: it works only on the addresses inside it.
  • Nothing is taken away at once: a site already showing the planner when 1.5.0 arrives keeps showing it for 30 days to add its key, and so does a site whose key has ended or been withdrawn. A new install starts in preview.
  • The key goes in Travel Planner > Settings > Licence key, or in the theme's gildhart-travel-planner.json ("licence"), or as GTP_LICENCE_KEY in wp-config.php; the settings win.
  • Vaccine pages: a site's own page about a vaccine can be named beside its price (Travel Planner > Settings, "Its page on this site"; "page" in the theme's file). The vaccine's name then links to it on every country's card and in every country guide, where a search engine reads it too. Only a page on the site itself, only while it is published, and never the page being shown; the settings screen says which are linked and which wait for their page. A vaccine with no page is plain text, as before.
  • Issuing and withdrawing keys: the "Licence keys" workflow (Actions > Licence keys > Run workflow), or tools/licence.php. Withdrawn keys are listed in the updates file, which every release carries on. A release is refused unless the plugin's public key is the signing secret's.
